title: Oregon Health & Science University (UO)
summary: Oregon Health & Science University (UO) is a university in Portland. This entry compiles College Scorecard figures and related sources; UniRepository is not affiliated with UO.

sections.heading: What UO is known for
paragraphs: Oregon Health & Science University is a public institution primarily recognized for its focus on health-related disciplines. The university's undergraduate enrollment stands at 836 students, reflecting its specialized academic environment. Health programs constitute the full share of the university's academic offerings, emphasizing its commitment to medical and health sciences education. While the university does not offer business programs, its dedication to health fields positions it as a key institution in this sector.

sections.heading: Key strengths
paragraphs: Oregon Health & Science University (UO) is a public institution distinguished by its exclusive focus on health-related academic programs. This concentrated approach highlights UO's commitment to advancing knowledge and training in health fields, setting it apart as a specialized public university.

sections.heading: Financial aid
paragraphs: Oregon Health & Science University (UO) offers financial aid to support students in managing educational expenses. Approximately 28.93% of students receive Pell Grants, which are federal subsidies for low-income students. Among those who complete their programs, the median debt is $16,625, reflecting the typical borrowing amount upon graduation. Prospective and current students can use the university's net price calculator available at www.ohsu.edu/ to estimate individual costs and aid eligibility. Additional financial data and resources are also accessible through the College Scorecard website.

sections.heading: Career outcomes
paragraphs: Career outcomes for graduates of Oregon Health & Science University (UO) indicate strong earning potential in health-related fields. The median earnings for alumni six years after completion of their programs is $99,818, increasing to $101,028 ten years post-completion. This suggests that UO graduates experience continued income growth as they advance in their careers. The median debt for those who complete their studies is $16,625, reflecting the typical financial investment required to obtain a degree from the university. While specific completion rates within 150% of the expected time are not available, the earnings data highlights the economic value of UO's specialized health programs.

sections.heading: Diversity
paragraphs: Oregon Health & Science University (UO) demonstrates a diverse student body with a majority of women, who constitute approximately 81.58% of the enrollment, while men make up about 18.42%. The racial and ethnic composition includes 62.44% White students, 20.57% Hispanic, 5.98% Asian, and 2.39% Black students. Additionally, nearly 29% of the student population receives Pell Grants, indicating a significant portion of students come from lower-income backgrounds. This demographic distribution reflects UO's commitment to fostering an inclusive academic environment within its health-focused programs.
